title: General-purpose synthesis of practical mechanisms

concept.text: The proposed innovation is a design system that converts practical requirements for motion, force, packaging, and durability into manufacturable mechanisms. Given a brief, it would choose an appropriate mechanism family, determine how its parts connect, and develop the dimensions and other design details needed to deliver the requested behavior. Its defining ambition is reliable selection across substantially different families, including linkages, compliant mechanisms, and cam or gear-based mechanisms.

In this proposed scope, selecting the arrangement of parts and joints is inseparable from solving geometry, dynamics, strength, tolerances, manufacturing, and, where needed, control. A mechanism that traces the desired path in an ideal model would still need to carry the specified loads, fit the available space, tolerate manufacturing variation, and operate for the required lifetime. The target is therefore a practical design capability extending from requirements through fabrication and validation. Whether existing systems already deliver this breadth remains unresolved in the supplied evidence.

significance.text: As a conditional assessment, reliable synthesis across mechanism families would substantially expand the range of mechanical design decisions that can be automated. It could reduce the expertise and effort needed to move from a functional requirement to a buildable mechanism, while making it easier to compare solutions that use different mechanical principles. The revolutionary claim concerns access to sophisticated design capability and the breadth of problems a system could handle; it does not depend on proving that a chosen mechanism is mathematically the simplest or globally optimal.

Plausible downstream benefits include faster development of robotic mechanisms, prosthetic devices, and industrial machinery. Those benefits would depend on usable requirement specification, trustworthy validation, manufacturing access, adoption, and the demands of each application. For example, satisfying a mechanism's motion and load requirements would not by itself establish the suitability of an entire prosthetic device or robot for its intended use. These are reasoned possibilities, not demonstrated outcomes or forecasts.

The scope also has physical and practical limits. Some combinations of motion, load, size, material, cost, and lifetime requirements cannot be satisfied together. A useful system would expose tradeoffs and communicate uncertainty rather than promise a solution to every brief. Broad synthesis would not imply universal mechanical problem solving, automatic discovery of new materials, or elimination of engineering judgment.

missing_breakthrough.text: The target breakthrough is reliable coordination of mechanism-family selection with detailed engineering under practical constraints. As an engineering synthesis of the proposed scope, the central difficulty is that the arrangement of components is a discrete choice, while dimensions, operating conditions, and many performance variables vary continuously. Changing the arrangement can change the available motions, force transmission, failure modes, and manufacturing options, so optimizing dimensions within one fixed family cannot by itself establish competence across families.

A further barrier is carrying a candidate design through mutually interacting requirements. Geometry and dynamics must remain consistent with strength, tolerances, packaging, and fabrication choices. Where control is necessary, the mechanism and controller must work together under the stated operating conditions. The proposed capability requires a way to detect when improving one property creates unacceptable consequences elsewhere, and to judge designs using models whose assumptions remain valid for the intended application.

Reliable treatment of feasibility and uncertainty is another unresolved capability within the proposal. Failing to find a design does not establish that no design exists, while a successful idealized simulation does not establish that a fabricated mechanism will meet its brief. The system would need to distinguish a verified conflict among requirements, an unsuccessful search, and a candidate whose performance remains uncertain. The supplied evidence does not establish which of these barriers have already been overcome by existing tools.

current_state.text: The supplied bibliography attributes a paper titled “A General Procedure for Basic Kinematic Chain Formation and Topology Selection for Planar Mechanisms” to Arthur Erdman, John Titus, Mahmud Suhaimi Ibrahim, and Sean Mather, in Designs, dated 27 April 2026, with DOI 10.3390/designs10030046. These are supplied bibliographic details. The source index records the article as not captured and contains no saved artifacts, so the review could not verify its identity or inspect its contents.

The research account describes this paper as offering a procedure for planar kinematic-chain selection, discussing limited general guidance for topology selection, and presenting examples narrower than the proposed end-to-end capability. Those descriptions remain unverified here because no article text was available in the supplied review. The title indicates apparent relevance to planar mechanism topology, but it cannot establish the procedure's effectiveness, the limits of its examples, or its relationship to broader practical synthesis.

The research also states that automated and optimization-based synthesis exists for restricted problems. The supplied review had no inspectable source passages supporting the scope or performance of those methods, so this record cannot substantiate particular demonstrated achievements, fabricated results, or quantitative performance levels. Its bounded search record was empty, leaving the current breadth of available systems unassessed. This evidence gap neither disproves the reported work nor establishes that general-purpose practical synthesis remains unavailable.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed evaluation: use a blinded collection of diverse, independently written briefs, with feasibility assessed through independent review. The collection should require solutions spanning at least linkages, compliant mechanisms, and cam or gear-based mechanisms, and should exercise motion, force, packaging, durability, and manufacturing constraints. Evaluation should establish that the system can select among families in response to requirements and produce sufficiently complete designs for fabrication. These are proposed criteria, not established standards.
completion_criteria.label: Select mechanism families and produce fabrication-ready designs from blinded briefs

completion_criteria.text: Fabricated examples should meet motion and load tolerances specified before testing and survive a defined endurance test under declared operating conditions. A reproducible demonstration should disclose the briefs, design outputs, relevant material and manufacturing assumptions, test procedures, measured results, and human intervention. Independent fabrication or testing of selected examples would strengthen confidence that success transfers beyond the original development setting. The tolerances and endurance requirements should be chosen for the applications being evaluated; the supplied record proposes no universal numerical thresholds.
completion_criteria.label: Fabricated mechanisms meet specified tolerances and survive defined endurance tests

completion_criteria.text: An independent comparison with experienced designers should assess design quality, cost, and design effort under comparable requirements and access to resources. Results should make clear how much expert assistance the system needed and where its outputs required correction. This proposed comparison would test the claimed practical gains in accessibility and development effort alongside mechanical performance.
completion_criteria.label: Independent comparison assesses quality, cost, and effort against experienced designers

completion_criteria.text: For briefs containing independently established conflicts, the system should identify or clearly qualify those conflicts rather than return a false guarantee. Where it merely fails to find a solution, it should preserve that distinction. Passing the evaluation would demonstrate capability within the tested mechanism families, operating conditions, constraint combinations, and distribution of briefs. Finite tests would not establish universal synthesis, complete detection of infeasibility, or reliability outside those demonstrated boundaries.
completion_criteria.label: Distinguish established constraint conflicts from search failures within stated limits

related_concepts.text: Based on the supplied roster, MEC-05, “Programmable solids that become different load-bearing mechanisms,” has the closest overlap in mechanism behavior. MEC-13 could include compliant or reconfigurable structures among its design options, whereas MEC-05 concerns solids capable of changing their load-bearing mechanical function. MEC-08, “Distributed actuators that simultaneously match skeletal muscle,” could supply actuation options for synthesized mechanisms; actuator performance and the ability to select and integrate actuators are distinct advances.

MEC-11, “Transferable prediction of wear and component life,” and MEC-12, “Predictive mechanics of real, evolving surface contacts,” could improve the durability and contact models used to evaluate candidate mechanisms. MEC-02, “Service-life superlubricity in ordinary machine contacts,” and MEC-04, “Ambient fatigue immunity in bulk structural metals,” concern changes in physical component performance that could expand the feasible design space. MEC-13 would need to work with the performance actually available and validated for its chosen materials and contacts; achieving synthesis would not establish these separate capabilities.

MEC-06, “Macroscopic atomically precise mechanosynthesis,” and MEC-09, “Mechanical self-replication of a production cell from feedstock,” overlap through manufacturing and production. A synthesis system might help design mechanisms used in such systems, but generating a manufacturable design does not demonstrate atomically precise fabrication or production-cell self-replication. MEC-07, “Bulk structural solids at a large fraction of ideal strength,” and MEC-10, “Stress-directed growth of load-bearing structures,” similarly concern material or structural capabilities that a design system might exploit if available.

MEC-01, “An engineering-predictive theory of turbulent flow,” could become relevant when synthesized mechanisms interact with fluids. MEC-03, “Engines that make sub-100 °C heat worth converting,” and MEC-14, “Low-cost mechanical storage with high efficiency over long periods,” are potential application areas for mechanical design. These relationships are inferred from the supplied titles: each retains its own physical and performance objectives, and success in mechanism synthesis would not establish success in those other innovations.

change_log.reason: These strengthen the proposed demonstration without presenting evaluation choices as consensus standards or finite testing as proof of universality.

unresolved_issues: The listed paper's bibliographic identity, procedure, examples, findings, and limitations remain unverified because no source artifact was captured.
The supplied record does not establish the current capabilities of restricted synthesis methods or whether any existing system already meets the proposed cross-family practical scope.
Freshness remains unassessed because the supplied bounded search record is empty.
Benchmark composition, feasibility adjudication, application-specific tolerances, endurance conditions, acceptable human intervention, and comparative scoring remain to be defined.
How reliably a system could distinguish infeasibility from search failure across substantially different mechanism families remains an open technical and evaluation question.

brief.title: Automatic design of working moving parts
possible: You could describe how something must move, how much force it must carry, where it must fit and how long it must last. A design system would turn that brief into plans for a mechanism: an arrangement of parts that produces the required movement.

It would choose between joined bars, parts that bend, and mechanisms driven by shaped rotating surfaces or toothed wheels. It would work out the connections, dimensions and manufacturing details needed to build and test the design.
why: This could reduce the specialist knowledge and effort needed to turn a functional requirement into something buildable. Designers could compare solutions that use different mechanical principles.
Developers of robots, prosthetic devices and industrial machinery could explore designs faster, with more of the detailed mechanical engineering handled automatically.

sources.who: Arthur Erdman, John Titus, Mahmud Suhaimi Ibrahim and Sean Mather
sources.showed: This paper describes a procedure for choosing arrangements of connected parts in mechanisms whose motion stays in a plane.
sources.cited_for: It addresses choosing how a mechanism's parts connect.
sources.not_established: It does not establish reliable selection across mechanism families or designs validated against full practical requirements.

sources.who: V. Megaro, J. Zehnder, M. Bächer, S. Coros, M. Gross and B. Thomaszewski
sources.showed: Their tool turns a supplied arrangement of rigid parts and joints into a mechanism that moves through bending. They manufactured physical prototypes.
sources.quote: We demonstrate our method on a set of examples that range from simple four-bar linkages to full-fledged animatronics, and verify the feasibility of our designs by manufacturing physical prototypes.
sources.cited_for: Automated design can produce buildable mechanisms that move through bending.
sources.not_established: The tool starts with a chosen arrangement; it does not establish selection across families or lifetime performance.

sources.who: Hao Xu, Tianwen Fu, Peng Song, Mingjun Zhou, Chi-Wing Fu and Niloy J. Mitra
sources.showed: Their method adjusts user-supplied shapes into working pairs of non-circular gears: toothed wheels with irregular outlines. They demonstrated designs in simulation and through physical printing.
sources.quote: Our optimized gears not only resemble the inputs but can also drive the motion with relatively small torque.
sources.cited_for: Automated gear design can connect shape requirements with motion and the turning force needed to drive it.
sources.not_established: The work addresses gear pairs, without establishing selection across families or endurance under a complete practical brief.

sources.who: Yayati Jadhav and Amir Barati Farimani
sources.showed: In a preprint, they describe a model that generates linkages, arrangements of rigid bars connected by joints, for a requested movement path. It chooses both connections and joint positions.
sources.quote:
We demonstrate this capability by successfully
synthesizing upto 20 node linkage systems but can be extended to N-nodes.
sources.cited_for: A model can choose connections and dimensions together within the linkage family.
sources.not_established: The reported results do not establish fabricated performance, durability or selection across different mechanism families.

shown: Megaro and collaborators manufactured prototypes of mechanisms that move through bending. Xu and collaborators designed and printed working non-circular gears. These tools demonstrate practical progress within particular mechanism families.
Jadhav and Farimani's preprint reports generating linkages with up to 20 joints from requested movement paths. It brings the choice of connections and dimensions together within that family.
missing: The target requires reliable selection across families while solving dimensions, strength, fit and manufacturing together.
Fabricated designs need to meet declared movement and load limits and survive application-specific endurance tests.
Independent comparisons need to establish design quality, cost and effort relative to experienced designers.
A system needs to distinguish conflicting requirements from an unsuccessful search or an uncertain candidate.

milestones.label: Unseen briefs yield buildable designs across mechanism families
milestones.explanation: A blinded evaluation would have to yield fabrication-ready designs spanning joined bars, bending parts, and cam or gear mechanisms under practical constraints. This would test selection across different mechanical principles.

milestones.label: Built mechanisms meet performance limits and survive endurance tests
milestones.explanation: Fabricated mechanisms would have to meet movement and load limits set before testing and survive declared endurance tests with reproducible results. This would connect design predictions to physical performance.

milestones.label: Independent comparison measures performance against experienced designers
milestones.explanation: An independent comparison would have to assess quality, cost and effort against experienced designers under comparable conditions, including expert corrections. This would test the claimed practical gains.

milestones.label: Conflicting requirements are distinguished from unsuccessful searches
milestones.explanation: Tests would have to show that the system identifies or qualifies established conflicts and distinguishes them from search failures. This would establish trustworthy limits within the tested conditions.

uncertain: It remains unclear whether any existing system already combines the full range of practical capabilities.
The breadth of test briefs, acceptable human assistance and application-specific performance thresholds remain to be defined.
How reliably can a system distinguish impossible requirements from a search that has missed a workable design?
